receipts.basis: Computer Matching Agreement, SSA Match #1016 / IRS Project #066 (DIFSLA), fully executed Oct 20 2025, effective Jan 1 2026 – Jun 30 2027. Under IRC § 6103(l)(7) the IRS discloses unearned-income information from the Information Returns Master File to SSA; SSA submits an SSN-based finder file (from the Supplemental Security Record), IRS matches it against information returns (e.g. Form 1099) and returns unearned-income records; SSA uses the result to verify SSI (Title XVI) eligibility and correct benefit amounts. FY2023 cost-benefit: ~$74.5M projected SSI benefit from overpayments recovered and ongoing payments corrected. Retrieval note: the source is a public PDF accessible to human review at the URL above; automated fetch returned HTTP 403, so this basis is PARAPHRASED and no direct quote was extracted by tooling. Facts corroborated against the SSA CMA index and IRS IRM 11.3.29 ([[r-difsla-irm]]). "Fetch failed" is not "source unreviewed."

IRS Internal Revenue Manual 11.3.29 (DIFSLA): "Pursuant to IRC 6103(l)(7)(B), the IRS shall disclose unearned income information from the IRMF [Information Returns Master File] to federal, state, and local agencies administering the federal benefit programs pursuant to the DIFSLA program." Recipient agencies may use the information "only to determine eligibility or to correct amount of benefits" and may not redisclose it to contractors; detailed request procedures are in IRS Publication 3373.

Computer Matching and Privacy Protection Act, 5 U.S.C. § 552a(p): an agency may not suspend, terminate, reduce, or make a final denial of a benefit to an individual as a result of information produced by a matching program until the agency has independently verified the information and provided the individual notice and a 30-day opportunity to contest. This is the statutory verify-before-adverse-action safeguard cited in the edge contestation blocks.

IRS newsroom statement on the proposed pilot-program regulations: "Treasury will make one-time $1,000 pilot program contributions to the Trump Accounts of eligible children for whom elections have been made." Eligibility: child "must be born in calendar year 2025, 2026, 2027, or 2028, be a United States citizen, [and] have been issued a Social Security Number." The statement does NOT describe how eligibility is verified or whether records are shared/matched between IRS, Treasury, and SSA — recorded here as absence, not concealment.

IRS Trump Accounts guidance: to establish an initial Trump account, the taxpayer signs in to their IRS Online Account — which uses ID.me identity verification — and submits Form 4547. ID.me is therefore the identity-proofing operator on the intake path. (Observed via agency guidance rather than direct page inspection: form.trumpaccounts.gov 301-redirects to irs.gov/trumpaccounts and the account flow is app/SPA-based.)

Treasury press release "Treasury Announces the Launch of the Trump Accounts App and Next Steps for Trump Accounts" (sb0508). Families open accounts by filing IRS Form 4547 on TrumpAccounts.gov; Treasury operates the Trump Accounts app; activation emails come only from no-reply@TrumpAccounts.Treasury.gov; Treasury deposits the one-time $1,000 contribution into eligible children's accounts beginning July 4, 2026.

Privacy Act SORN, "Department of the Treasury, .031 — Trump Accounts Program (TAP) System of Records" (FR 2026-07514, Apr 17 2026). The system "supports the Treasury's administration, oversight and compliance activities associated with Trump accounts," a type of traditional IRA under 26 U.S.C. 530A; records "enable Treasury to administer and oversee program operations, ensure compliance with applicable statutory requirements, and carry out the objectives for Trump accounts."

cases.title: IRS/SSA DIFSLA (Match #1016) — SSI recipients matched against IRS unearned-income records
cases.headline: How SSI recipients become an IRS income match
cases.dek: SSA sends recipient identifiers to the IRS, which matches them against information-return records and returns unearned-income data used to verify SSI eligibility and benefit amounts — a written computer matching agreement, not an inference.
cases.why: This is documented composition: a benefit recipient's identifier is joined to IRS income records by agreement, and the result can reduce or recover their payment. The same match has recurred since 2000, with a statutory safeguard requiring SSA to verify and notice before any adverse action.

cases.title: TrumpAccounts.gov / Form 4547 — child + guardian intake into the Treasury TAP system of records
cases.headline: How a child-savings form becomes a joinable government record
cases.dek: Documented records show TrumpAccounts.gov and IRS Form 4547 collecting a child's and a guardian's identity — including both Social Security numbers — and routing them into a Treasury system of record that drives pilot-eligibility and oversight decisions.
cases.why: These are not just values. They are join keys: stable identifiers and relationship fields that can link a child, a household, a tax filer, benefit eligibility, and account administration into one composable record.
cases.summary: TrumpAccounts.gov collects child and parent/guardian identity (including both SSNs) via IRS Form 4547 to open a Trump account (a § 530A IRA) and elect a one-time $1,000 Treasury pilot contribution. Intake is identity-proofed through ID.me and lands in Treasury's ".031 — Trump Accounts Program (TAP)" Privacy Act system of records, which exists for administration, oversight, and compliance. The statute directs Treasury to disburse the $1,000, but no public document witnesses how the eligibility records move IRS→Treasury or are matched against SSA — so those edges are AUTHORIZED, not documented. The composed parent↔child identity linkage is an inferred household graph.
